---
title: Your first Tooee app
description: Write a screen with a row list, a hotkey, and chrome on the Tooee shell, then run it with bun.
---

```tsx title="app.tsx"
import { launchCli, useQuitCommand } from "@tooee/shell";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

const ReleaseChecklist = function ReleaseChecklist(): ReactNode {
  useQuitCommand();
  return <text content="Release checklist. Press q to quit." />;
};

await launchCli(<ReleaseChecklist />);
```

```bash
bun add @tooee/shell @tooee/commands @tooee/layout @tooee/themes
bun app.tsx
```

`launchCli` creates an OpenTUI renderer, mounts `TooeeProvider` around your component, and returns when the renderer is ready. The provider gives the tree modes, commands, themes, overlays, toasts, and config. `useQuitCommand` registers `q` in cursor mode; `ctrl+c` ends the process from any mode. `<text>` is an [OpenTUI](https://opentui.com) element; the JSX options from [Install](/docs/start/install#set-the-jsx-options) make it typecheck.

The rest of this page grows `app.tsx` until it has a row list with a cursor, a hotkey, and a title bar and status bar.

## Add rows and a cursor

```tsx title="app.tsx"
import { launchCli, useNavigation, useQuitCommand } from "@tooee/shell";
import { useTheme } from "@tooee/themes";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

const checklist = ["Run the tests", "Bump the version", "Write the changelog", "Tag the release"];

const ReleaseChecklist = function ReleaseChecklist(): ReactNode {
  const { theme } = useTheme();
  const { cursor } = useNavigation({ rowCount: checklist.length });
  useQuitCommand();

  return (
    <box flexDirection="column" paddingLeft={1}>
      {checklist.map(
        (item, index): ReactNode => (
          <text
            key={item}
            content={`${index === cursor ? ">" : " "} ${item}`}
            fg={index === cursor ? theme.primary : theme.text}
          />
        ),
      )}
    </box>
  );
};

await launchCli(<ReleaseChecklist />);
```

`useNavigation({ rowCount })` registers the cursor keys from [Keyboard basics](/docs/start/keyboard-basics#move): `j`, `k`, `ctrl+d`, `ctrl+u`, `g g`, `G`, and `v` for select mode. It returns the state your component draws from:

| Field            | Type                                     | Meaning                                                  |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cursor`         | `number \| null`                         | Index of the cursor row. Starts at `0`.                  |
| `selection`      | `{ start: number; end: number } \| null` | The row range in select mode.                            |
| `toggledIndices` | `Set<number>`                            | Rows toggled with `Tab` when `multiSelect` is on.        |
| `setCursor`      | `(index: number) => void`                | Move the cursor from code, for example on a mouse click. |

The hook owns the cursor and the keys. Your component owns the rows and the way a row looks. `useTheme` from `@tooee/themes` returns the active theme, and `theme.primary` and `theme.text` follow the theme picker.

Options: `isSelectable(index)` returns `false` for rows the cursor skips, `multiSelect: true` turns on `Tab` toggling, and `viewportHeight` sets the size of a half page for `ctrl+d` and `ctrl+u`.

## Add a command with a hotkey

```tsx title="app.tsx"
import { useCommand } from "@tooee/commands";
import { launchCli, useNavigation, useQuitCommand } from "@tooee/shell";
import { useTheme } from "@tooee/themes";
import { useState } from "react";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

const checklist = ["Run the tests", "Bump the version", "Write the changelog", "Tag the release"];

const ReleaseChecklist = function ReleaseChecklist(): ReactNode {
  const { theme } = useTheme();
  const { cursor } = useNavigation({ rowCount: checklist.length });
  const [done, setDone] = useState<ReadonlySet<number>>(new Set());
  useQuitCommand();
  useCommand({
    handler: () => {
      if (cursor === null) {
        return;
      }
      setDone((previous) => {
        const next = new Set(previous);
        if (next.has(cursor)) {
          next.delete(cursor);
        } else {
          next.add(cursor);
        }
        return next;
      });
    },
    hotkey: "x",
    id: "checklist.toggle",
    modes: ["cursor"],
    title: "Toggle done",
  });

  return (
    <box flexDirection="column" paddingLeft={1}>
      {checklist.map(
        (item, index): ReactNode => (
          <text
            key={item}
            content={`${index === cursor ? ">" : " "} [${done.has(index) ? "x" : " "}] ${item}`}
            fg={index === cursor ? theme.primary : theme.text}
          />
        ),
      )}
    </box>
  );
};

await launchCli(<ReleaseChecklist />);
```

`useCommand` registers one command for as long as the component is mounted. `id` names it, `title` is the text the command palette shows, `hotkey` binds a key, and `modes` limits it to cursor mode. The handler reads `cursor` from the render it was registered in; Tooee calls the latest handler, so the closure is never stale. Press `:` and type `tog` to find `Toggle done` in the palette. [Commands and modes](/docs/build/commands-and-modes) covers the hotkey grammar, sequences, leader keys, and modes.

## Add the chrome

```tsx title="app.tsx"
import { useCommand, useMode } from "@tooee/commands";
import { AppLayout } from "@tooee/layout";
import { launchCli, useNavigation, useQuitCommand } from "@tooee/shell";
import { useTheme } from "@tooee/themes";
import { useState } from "react";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

const checklist = ["Run the tests", "Bump the version", "Write the changelog", "Tag the release"];

const ReleaseChecklist = function ReleaseChecklist(): ReactNode {
  const { theme } = useTheme();
  const mode = useMode();
  const { cursor } = useNavigation({ rowCount: checklist.length });
  const [done, setDone] = useState<ReadonlySet<number>>(new Set());
  useQuitCommand();
  useCommand({
    handler: () => {
      if (cursor === null) {
        return;
      }
      setDone((previous) => {
        const next = new Set(previous);
        if (next.has(cursor)) {
          next.delete(cursor);
        } else {
          next.add(cursor);
        }
        return next;
      });
    },
    hotkey: "x",
    id: "checklist.toggle",
    modes: ["cursor"],
    title: "Toggle done",
  });

  return (
    <AppLayout
      titleBar={{ title: "Release checklist", subtitle: "0.9.0" }}
      statusBar={{
        items: [
          { label: "Done:", value: `${done.size}/${checklist.length}` },
          { label: "Mode:", value: mode },
          { label: "", value: "j/k move  x toggle  q quit" },
        ],
      }}
    >
      <box flexDirection="column" paddingLeft={1}>
        {checklist.map(
          (item, index): ReactNode => (
            <text
              key={item}
              content={`${index === cursor ? ">" : " "} [${done.has(index) ? "x" : " "}] ${item}`}
              fg={index === cursor ? theme.primary : theme.text}
            />
          ),
        )}
      </box>
    </AppLayout>
  );
};

await launchCli(<ReleaseChecklist />);
```

This is the complete file. `AppLayout` from `@tooee/layout` draws a title bar at the top, your content in the middle, and a status bar at the bottom. It also draws the current overlay and the toasts, so the command palette opens inside it. `titleBar` takes `title` and an optional `subtitle`. `statusBar.items` is a list of `{ label, value }` pairs; a muted label sits before each value. `useMode` from `@tooee/commands` returns the current mode, `cursor` here until you press `v`. [Layout and chrome](/docs/build/layout) covers the scroll and search bar options.

Run it:

```bash
bun app.tsx
```

Move with `j` and `k`, press `x` on a row, and watch the `Done:` count change. Press `v` and the status bar shows `select`; `Escape` returns to cursor mode. Press `:` for the palette and `q` to quit.

## Grow into a document

`useNavigation` stops at the cursor and the selection. When rows need search, copy, mouse clicks, and a right-click menu, hand them to the document controller instead:

```tsx title="checklist-document.tsx"
import { Document, DocumentScreen, launchCli, useDocumentController } from "@tooee/shell";
import { useState } from "react";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

const checklist = ["Run the tests", "Bump the version", "Write the changelog", "Tag the release"];

const ReleaseChecklist = function ReleaseChecklist(): ReactNode {
  const [done, setDone] = useState<ReadonlySet<number>>(new Set());
  const controller = useDocumentController({
    adapter: { getText: (item: string) => item },
    rows: checklist,
    search: {},
  });

  return (
    <DocumentScreen
      controller={controller}
      titleBar={{ title: "Release checklist" }}
      statusItems={[{ label: "Done:", value: `${done.size}/${checklist.length}` }]}
      actions={[
        {
          handler: () => {
            const index = controller.activeIndex;
            if (index === null) {
              return;
            }
            setDone((previous) => {
              const next = new Set(previous);
              if (next.has(index)) {
                next.delete(index);
              } else {
                next.add(index);
              }
              return next;
            });
          },
          hotkey: "x",
          id: "checklist.toggle",
          title: "Toggle done",
        },
      ]}
    >
      <Document
        controller={controller}
        style={{ flexGrow: 1 }}
        renderRow={(item, index): ReactNode => (
          <text content={` [${done.has(index) ? "x" : " "}] ${item}`} />
        )}
      />
    </DocumentScreen>
  );
};

await launchCli(<ReleaseChecklist />);
```

`useDocumentController` takes the rows and an adapter that says how to read each row as text. It registers the same cursor keys plus `/` search, `n` and `N`, and `y y` copy, and it highlights the cursor row itself. `DocumentScreen` wraps `AppLayout`, registers your `actions`, adds the `q` and `t` commands, and fills the status bar with the theme, the mode, and the cursor. `Document` draws one row per item with your `renderRow`. [Documents](/docs/build/documents) explains the adapter, row keys, search, and mouse options. [source-aware-document.tsx](https://github.com/gingerhendrix/tooee/blob/main/examples/shell/source-aware-document.tsx) is the same shape with rows that remember their source lines.
